high intensity running restored attention more than low intensity running, which in turn restored attention more than a resting condition.
high intensity running restored attention more than low intensity running and the comparison resting control group.
high intensity running restored attentional fatigue more effectively than low intensity running, self-regulated running and a control group that did not run.

the effects of running on attentional fatigue.
how the physical and psychological benefits of exercise are related.
how the level of intensity of physical activity affects attentional recovery, and how physical activity can be used to restore attention.

the results of this study support the hypothesis that high intensity running restores attentional fatigue more than a resting control group.

running intensity does not appear to be a significant factor in the recovery of attention from attentional fatigue, but that the level of physical activity does appear to be a contributing factor in the restoration of attention.

running at a high intensity level is more beneficial to the restoration of attention than running at a low intensity level.
the effects of running on attentional restoration are dependent on the intensity of the running.
running at a self-regulated intensity level for 20 minutes, in a natural setting, restored attention more effectively than the control group and running at low intensity.

high intensity running can be a useful strategy for restoring attentional fatigue.
